title: Production scheduler fairness primitives: WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision contracts
description:
Objective: land the production scheduler fairness primitives — WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision contracts — under packages/scheduler/src/fairness/**, so that task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production) has a real subject to implement against instead of a DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference that excludes the very structures it needs.

CREATED BY governor-f70d1157 at human direction on 2026-08-10, to the SPECIFICATION WRITTEN BY governor-42b952c9 in their audit comment on task-10cab3e5. That audit is the authority for this task's shape; read it. A governor created this task; an ARCHITECT must plan it. Nothing below is a plan.

WHY THIS EXISTS — IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT CAN CLEAR A PERMANENT DEAD END. governor-42b952c9's audit states it plainly: "THIS BLOCK CAN NEVER CLEAR ON ITS OWN... the condition that would satisfy this block has no owner and no existence. That makes this a PERMANENT DEAD END by construction, not a task that is merely waiting." The remedy was routed to #architects on 2026-08-09, the channel had hit its chat loop guard and returned routingTargets: [] so nobody was notified, and the fleet went down before it was re-routed. architect-8c9073cd, who was to author it, is no longer registered.

BLAST RADIUS — five tasks, the entire expansion tail of epic-e0c54bddb, queue behind this: task-10cab3e5 (Fair scheduler production), task-005c9896 (Expansion admission protocol), task-2561a780 (Scheduler expansion admission), task-b863bae8 (Expansion manual approval binding), task-a1e7f75e (Expansion protocol public hardening). Two more sit behind those: task-cda6bddf (Same-bug circuit breaker) and task-dddfaf83 (Graph supersession engine).

MEASURED ON DISK by governor-f70d1157 at 06:35Z on 2026-08-10, independently of the audit. Verify every line before trusting it:
- There is NO WDRR, ring, deficit-round or resource-queue production code anywhere under packages/scheduler/src. The directory holds admission/, authority/, budget/, convergence/, dependencies/, frontier, graph analysis and determinism modules — and nothing implementing fairness rotation.
- packages/scheduler/src/fairness/ DOES NOT EXIST. This task creates it.
- The reference model is docs/plans/2026-08-07-fable-fairness-aging-reference.md, banner line 1: "DEVELOPMENT_ONLY / NOT_CONFIRMATORY". Its executable form lives in packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/ — fairness-model.ts, fairness-codec.ts, fairness-lifecycle.ts, fairness-internal.ts, fairness-input.ts and their tests.
- Commit d33240c ("fix: harden fairness reference contracts") is the only correction candidate and carries no independent closure artifact.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — DO NOT DERIVE THE CONTRACTS FROM THE REFERENCE MODEL. The block on task-10cab3e5 is explicit that the landed DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference EXCLUDES the WDRR rings and resource queues, trusts caller-declared bypass IDs, and retains hostile-state gaps. Copying it forward would import those gaps into production and is the Clause 2 failure both governors named. Measure the gap SYMBOL BY SYMBOL ON DISK and design the production contracts to close it; consult the reference for vocabulary and counterexamples, never as the source of authority.

NOT IN SCOPE, and this list is binding: implementing the WDRR rotation algorithm itself or the aging policy (that is task-10cab3e5, which consumes these contracts); provider launch; graph mutation; changing fairness constants (task-10cab3e5's own rail forbids that without approval, and it applies here too); modifying packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/** — the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference stays as it is and is not promoted to production.

THIS TASK SHIPS CONTRACTS, NOT A SCHEDULER. If you find yourself implementing rotation, deficit accounting or aging decisions, you have crossed into task-10cab3e5's scope.

Per Clause 1, name task-10cab3e5 as the consumer in the plan and record its id.

Hard dependencies: none. Readiness explanation engine, Lease presence core and Conserved budget core — three of task-10cab3e5's four named dependencies — are all DONE.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm typecheck, plus a plain-Node import probe of whatever this publishes on the @moe/scheduler root.

Size: if the plan exceeds 12 steps or 10 distinct affectedFiles, SPLIT it and say so rather than padding. Five contract families is a plausible split boundary.
definitionOfDone: packages/scheduler/src/fairness/ exists and declares the five production contract families named by the governor audit — WorkItem, ring, resource, opportunity-evidence and cap-revision — as immutable types plus frozen stable reason-code vocabularies. Each family's shape is justified in planningNotes against a symbol-by-symbol disk measurement, NOT derived from the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference.

The three defects the reference is recorded as carrying are closed by construction in the production contracts, and each is proven by a test asserting the specific stable reason code AND the refusing layer per epic rail 6: (a) caller-declared bypass IDs are NOT trusted — a bypass claim the caller cannot prove is REFUSED, never admitted; (b) rings and resource queues are representable rather than excluded; (c) the hostile-state gaps the reference retains are either closed or recorded as typed UNKNOWN with the missing input named.
Every refusal path is total and the case sweep asserts it generated a non-zero number of cases, so an emptied sweep cannot pass silently.

The contracts carry NO authority and NO policy: a test asserts no exported function decides rotation order, deficit accounting or aging — those belong to the consumer task-10cab3e5. Contracts describe and validate; they do not schedule.
packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/** is UNCHANGED — git diff shows zero modifications there. The DEVELOPMENT_ONLY reference is consulted, never promoted to production and never edited.

Whatever this publishes is reachable from the @moe/scheduler package root, proven by a PLAIN-NODE import probe recorded verbatim — not by vitest, which resolves NodeNext .js specifiers back to .ts and is blind to a missing bridge. Clause 1: exporting into a directory is not composition.

task-10cab3e5 is named as the consumer in the plan per Clause 1. pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0, with foreign red attributed by path per global rail 3 and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: DO NOT DERIVE THE CONTRACTS FROM THE DEVELOPMENT_ONLY REFERENCE. It explicitly excludes the WDRR rings and resource queues this task must express, trusts caller-declared bypass IDs, and retains hostile-state gaps. Copying it forward imports those defects into production — the exact Clause 2 failure two governors independently named. Read it for vocabulary and counterexamples; measure the gap on disk and design the closure.

CONTRACTS ONLY — no rotation algorithm, no deficit accounting, no aging decisions. Those are task-10cab3e5's scope and it consumes what you build. If a DoD item seems to require scheduling behaviour, you have crossed the boundary: report blocked rather than widening.
Do not edit packages/testkit/src/scheduler-fairness/**. The reference stays DEVELOPMENT_ONLY and is not promoted. A diff touching it is a rejection.

Do not change fairness constants. task-10cab3e5's rail forbids it without approval and the same restraint binds here — constants are a product decision, not an implementation choice. If the contracts appear to require a constant that does not exist, report blocked and name it.

Fail closed with stable reason codes and the refusing layer, per epic rail 4 and rail 6. A bypass claim that cannot be proven is REFUSED; an input that cannot be classified is typed UNKNOWN with the missing evidence named, never optimistically admitted.

Read packages/scheduler/src/ end to end before naming a symbol — admission/, authority/, budget/ and convergence/ already exist and may already own vocabulary you would otherwise duplicate. Verify on disk (skill: explore-before-assume); this description was written by a governor from greps.
Keep each production source focused: target <=250 physical lines, split before 400. Five contract families will not fit one file.

Commit by explicit pathspec only — never git add -A. After `git add`, run `git diff --cached --name-only` and confirm the list is EXACTLY your owned paths: the git index is shared on this board and a foreign package.json arrived pre-staged in a governor commit earlier in this session.
